summary: Case pdf_slips_and_bank: 3 documents analysed; 7 finding(s) about the documents (5 high, 1 medium, 1 low) and 2 coverage note(s). Most significant: C-001 Salary slip arithmetic does not balance in salary_slip_tampered; X-001 Payslips for the same employee and month show different net pay; X-003 Salary slip net pay does not match bank payroll credit; X-002 Salary slip net pay does not match bank payroll credit. Visual findings are indicators of possible alteration, not proof; confirm against originals. Pixel-level visual forensics ran on 0 of 3 recognised page(s); PDF structure checks (fonts, overlays, hidden text, file history) ran on 3 generated PDF page(s), where pixel analysis does not apply.

findings.title: Amount in a different font from the other amounts in salary_slip_tampered
findings.explanation: '95,000' is set in Times-Roman, while 5 other amounts on the page use helvetica. A figure typed over another in a different typeface can look like this. It can also be a deliberate emphasis; this is an indicator only, so compare with the original.

findings.title: Salary slip arithmetic does not balance in salary_slip_tampered
findings.explanation: Gross 70,000 - deductions 10,000 = 60,000, but Net Pay shows 95,000 (difference +35,000). Corroborated by visual evidence (V-001) on the same field.

findings.title: Payslips for the same employee and month show different net pay
findings.explanation: salary_slip_clean: 60,000; salary_slip_tampered: 95,000 (employee TST-10234, 2026-10). Two payslips for one month should agree; either one was changed or they come from different sources. This is a data conflict to verify with the employer, not proof of fraud. Corroborated by visual evidence (V-001) on the same field.

findings.title: Salary slip net pay does not match bank payroll credit
findings.explanation: Net pay on salary_slip_clean is 60,000, but the payroll credit in the bank statement (bank_statement_conflict) on 2026-10-31 is 52,000 (difference +8,000). Either the payslip or the bank record is wrong; this is a data inconsistency to verify with the employer and the bank, not proof of fraud.

findings.title: Salary slip net pay does not match bank payroll credit
findings.explanation: Net pay on salary_slip_tampered is 95,000, but the payroll credit in the bank statement (bank_statement_conflict) on 2026-10-31 is 52,000 (difference +43,000). Either the payslip or the bank record is wrong; this is a data inconsistency to verify with the employer and the bank, not proof of fraud. Corroborated by visual evidence (V-001) on the same field.

findings.title: Running balance does not reconcile in bank_statement_conflict (1 of 1 rows)
findings.explanation: Each row's balance must equal the previous balance plus deposits minus withdrawals. row 3 (2026-10-31): previous balance 40,870.00 + credit 52,000.00 = 92,870.00, but the statement prints 93,990.00 (difference +1,120.00) A single altered amount or balance breaks this chain.

findings.title: Part of the transaction table in bank_statement_conflict could not be read
findings.explanation: 1 of 3 table rows have no readable amount or balance, so the running-balance check covered 1 rows only.

findings.title: Pages salary_slip_clean and salary_slip_tampered are near-identical
findings.explanation: The printed content of the two pages overlaps 100% (different pages score below 80%, even with the same layout): the same document may have been submitted twice, or a page was copied. A copy with one value changed also scores this high.

findings.title: Pixel-level forensics not applicable to 3 born-digital PDF page(s)
findings.explanation: These pages are generated PDFs (text layer, no scanned image), so compression/grain/ink analysis does not apply. Their exact text was read from the PDF (no OCR), and PDF structure checks were run instead: font consistency of amounts, bordered patches and covered or hidden text, and file history. Content checks (arithmetic, formats, cross-document) were run as for any page. A clean result is not proof of authenticity: a document can be forged before it is turned into a PDF. Pages: bank_statement_conflict, salary_slip_clean, salary_slip_tampered

confidence_scale: Confidence levels: high (0.80 and above), medium (0.60 to 0.79), low (below 0.60). The number is the system's own estimate of how reliable the specific check is on this evidence (for example an exact arithmetic mismatch scores high, a weak pixel signal scores low). It is not a probability that a document is forged, and it does not say which of two conflicting documents is correct.

standards.note: This system draws on the frameworks below as reference points. It does not claim compliance or certification with any of them; each row says what we do and what we do not do.

rows.framework: ISO/IEC 27037 (identification, collection, acquisition and preservation of digital evidence)
rows.what_we_do: Each source file is hashed (SHA-256) at ingest; originals are never modified (analysis uses derived copies, recorded in the log); every step is written to a hash-chained audit log with archived run history.
rows.what_we_do_not: No acquisition or custody control before upload: the system only sees the copy it is given. No write protection or collection records for the original device or system.

rows.framework: ISO/IEC 27041 (suitability and adequacy of investigative methods)
rows.what_we_do: Methods are documented (ARCHITECTURE.md), tested on a synthetic benchmark and a separately generated synthetic test pack with an answer key, and limitations are stated openly (skilled forgeries, tuning on synthetic data).
rows.what_we_do_not: No formal validation study, no measured error rates on real documents, no independent testing.

rows.framework: ISO/IEC 27042 (analysis and interpretation of digital evidence)
rows.what_we_do: Findings separate a data inconsistency, a potential alteration and an observation; each has a confidence level, possible explanations and a suggested check; nothing is called fraud; the pipeline is deterministic and repeatable.
rows.what_we_do_not: Confidence levels are the system's own estimates, not calibrated probabilities; no formal competence or review process around the analyst.

rows.framework: NIST SP 800-86 (forensic techniques in incident response)
rows.what_we_do: The pipeline follows its collection, examination, analysis and reporting phases: ingest and hashing; reading, extraction, structure and forensic checks; contextual and cross-document analysis; the dossier.
rows.what_we_do_not: It is written for incident response on live systems; volatile data, network and system sources are out of scope here.

rows.what_we_do: No training is done and no model is hosted, so model theft, poisoning, inversion and membership inference do not apply. Supply chain: the downloaded embedding model is checked against recorded SHA-256 values and the result is logged. Output integrity: hash-chained audit and review logs. The optional Claude summary is off by default.
rows.what_we_do_not: Input manipulation (documents crafted to mislead OCR or classification) is only partly mitigated (veto rule, minimum expected fields) and not tested adversarially. Recorded model hashes were taken from our own first download, not from a publisher signature. RapidOCR models are bundled in their package and not separately pinned. When the optional summary is on, finding text (document values) is sent to an external API.

V-001.label: Potential alteration: an indicator that something may have been changed, not proof
V-001.why: The way this PDF was built (fonts, drawing order, hidden layers, file history) differs from an untouched generated document.
V-001.check: Request the native or re-issued file from the issuer, inspect the region at full size and compare the two.
explanations: A legitimate correction re-issued by the issuer
A design element (badge, highlight) that looks like a patch
A value overwritten after the document was generated

C-001.label: Confirmed data conflict: two values in the submitted documents contradict each other (this says nothing about intent)
C-001.why: Figures printed on the same page do not add up, so at least one of them is wrong or was changed after the document was produced.
C-001.check: Ask the issuer for the original or a recalculation and compare the figures with the payroll record.
explanations: A typing or calculation error when the document was produced
One figure edited after the document was produced
A different version of the statement mixed with this one

X-001.label: Confirmed data conflict: two values in the submitted documents contradict each other (this says nothing about intent)
X-001.why: Documents that describe the same person or application disagree; at most one of them can be right.
X-001.check: Obtain the originals of the documents named, find which one matches the issuer's record, and do not assume which is correct.
explanations: A typing error in one of the documents
The documents were produced at different times or are different versions
A value in one document was changed
A document of another person was mixed in

X-002.label: Confirmed data conflict: two values in the submitted documents contradict each other (this says nothing about intent)
X-002.why: Records that should agree (payslip, bank statement, application, case reference) show different values.
X-002.check: Obtain the bank's own statement and the employer's payroll or confirmation record and see which side matches the issuer's data.
explanations: Timing: the payslip was corrected or reissued after the bank credit
Net pay shown before an adjustment that the bank reflects
A figure on the payslip or in the bank record was changed

X-003.label: Confirmed data conflict: two values in the submitted documents contradict each other (this says nothing about intent)
X-003.why: Records that should agree (payslip, bank statement, application, case reference) show different values.
X-003.check: Obtain the bank's own statement and the employer's payroll or confirmation record and see which side matches the issuer's data.
explanations: Timing: the payslip was corrected or reissued after the bank credit
Net pay shown before an adjustment that the bank reflects
A figure on the payslip or in the bank record was changed

T-001.label: Confirmed data conflict: two values in the submitted documents contradict each other (this says nothing about intent)
T-001.why: A value breaks a rule that should hold within this document (format, date logic, balance or total).
T-001.check: Verify the value against the original document and the issuing authority.
explanations: A typing or calculation error when the document was produced
One figure edited after the document was produced
A different version of the statement mixed with this one

T-002.label: Observation: a note, coverage gap or weak signal, not an accusation
T-002.why: A check could not be completed or a value could not be read, so the absence of findings here is not evidence that the page is genuine.
T-002.check: Review the field or page manually, or resubmit a clearer capture.
explanations: Poor capture, faint print or an unusual layout
The information is genuinely absent from the document

T-003.label: Observation: a note, coverage gap or weak signal, not an accusation
T-003.why: A value breaks a rule that should hold within this document (format, date logic, balance or total).
T-003.check: Verify the value against the original document and the issuing authority.
explanations: A second party or column (for example year-to-date) printed next to the first
The page or row was copied or overwritten

N-001.label: Observation: a note, coverage gap or weak signal, not an accusation
N-001.why: A check could not be completed or a value could not be read, so the absence of findings here is not evidence that the page is genuine.
